title: How to Perform Inference in Spark with an XGBoost Model Trained in scikit-learn?
question:
I found one xgboost model which was trained using sklearn in native python. How can I use that model to produce inference on new dataset in pyspark?

Apart from using UDFs, what other options do I have?
answer:
There's a deprecated spark_sklearn package but it was superseded by joblib-spark which unfortunately doesn't support distributed inference. So I guess your best bet is to use pandas_udf:

@F.pandas_udf(returnType=DoubleType())
def predict(*cols):
    X = pd.concat(cols, axis=1) # cols is a tuple of pd.Series
    return pd.Series(model.predict_proba(X)[:, 1])

df_labeled = df.select(
    F.col('id'),
    predict(*column_names).alias('proba')
)

Of course there will still be some overhead here, but generally pandas_udf are efficient enough so that this overhead is negligible compared to the actual inference time (and Spark overhead)
